title.narrative: NRC Collaboration across Societies for Peace, Inclusion, and Resilience (CASPIR)
NRC Collaboration across Societies for Peace, Inclusion, and Resilience (CASPIR)

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the CASPIR project is improved peaceful, sustainable, and dignified living conditions for displacement-affected communities as result of enhanced, diversified, and more adaptable livelihoods productivity, enhanced financial inclusion and strengthened market systems.
The specific outcome objectives are:
Outcome 1: Support pathways towards sustainable peace through a more inclusive, community centred process with greater participation of women.; and
Outcome 2: Support to agriculture production systems through sustainable and diversified practices to foster increased production, food security, and access to markets.

Det övergripande målet med interventionen är att främja säkra, hållbara och värdiga levnadsvillkor för fördrivna människor i konfliktdrabbade områden. Projektet syftar till att stärka användandet av landtillgångar och samtidigt stärka samhälles möjligheter att använda land för inkomstbringande aktiviteter. Projektet avses implementeras i delstaterna Södra Kordofan och White Nile.

The overall objective of the intervention is to foster safe, sustainable, and dignified living conditions for displacement-affected communities prone to conflict over natural resources and due to inadequate adaptable and diversified livelihood options resulting in additional barrier in accessing basic services. The project will be implemented in South Kordofan State and White Nile State.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
Despite a very challenging context, the project has succeeded in making good progress towards the targets for most of the indicators in the projects results framework. This update is based on reporting on progress until April 2025 and consist of selected, and slight edited, extracts from the Norwegian Refugee Council's (NRC) annual reporting for the period May 2024 to April 2025. Examples of progress include NRC's team for Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) actively engaging women from project communities in White Nile to strengthen their knowledge of Housing, Land and Property (HLP) and Legal Civil Documentation (LCD) rights. A total of 27 women from farmer committees formed participated in a Community Dispute Resolution (CDR) training. Additionally, 27 midwives from the target areas took part in LCD training sessions. In South Kordofan 14 midwives and 15 women from the agricultural committees benefited from the CDR and Legal Identity Documentation (LID) trainings. These efforts aim to empower women to understand and confidently exercise their rights, while also supporting others to do the same. By overcoming discriminatory practiceswith the backing of community leaders and committees who participated in the trainings and expressed a willingness to support womenthe programme seeks to promote greater inclusion and access to housing, land, and property (HLP) rights by resolving property disputes, especially on share cropping arrangements or land access issues that might emerge from the use of the land for agricultural purposes. Additionally, the LID training sought to equip midwives with the knowledge and tools to play a critical role in documenting births within their respective communities. This interim measure is essential to ensure that vital data is not lost due to the absence of or delays in the Civil Registry operations. It will also facilitate the registration process once Civil Registry services are restored.
NRC, through its ICLA team and implementing partner in White Nile and South Kordofan states, provided information services to 13,489 (9450 F, 4039M) individuals. These sessions aimed to raise awareness on the various types of legal identity documents and the procedural requirements for obtaining new documents or replacement national numbers and birth and marriage certificates. In addition, individual counselling services on legal identity and civil documentation were delivered to a total of 13,129 (8217F, 4912M) individuals. These one-on-one sessions focused on informing participants about the specific steps and requirements for obtaining essential civil documentation and legal identity documents.
Legal assistance services were provided to 150 (75F, 75M) individuals in South Kordofan who were supported to obtain marriage certificates in collaboration with the Judiciary. Support provided included hands-on guidance on completing the necessary administrative forms and securing the documents required for the application. In White Nile, 1,069 individuals requiring birth registration were identified and referred to the Civil registry office. The documents are issued upon completion. The standard processing period is approximately one month.
During the reporting period, NRC supported 406 farmers (101F, 305M) with seed vouchers valued at 120 USD each, totalling 48,720 USD in disbursed support. Additionally, four Farmers Field Schools were established across Kosti and Rabak localities. A demonstration plot was set up at each school to support practical training. NRC supported the demonstration plots by providing seeds, tools, and farming services such as ploughing. To ensure effective learning and adoption of improved practices, technical training was delivered to all participants on cultivation and post-harvest management. These sessions were facilitated by agricultural ministry specialists alongside trained community extension workers.
On the environmental front, the Livelihoods and Food Security team identified and established eight environmental committees. These committees were formed to promote sustainable natural resource management, raise awareness on environmental protection practices, and support community-led efforts to mitigate environmental degradation. As part of their engagement, committee members developed environmental action plans outlining various initiatives to support local ecosystems. Based on these plans, NRC selected 12 initiatives across six communities for direct support, primarily focusing on afforestation and the establishment of community nurseries. Furthermore, 25 environmental awareness campaigns were organized and facilitated across the targeted locations to strengthen community knowledge and engagement in environmental conservation. To support agropastoral access to market, 47 early adaptors were identified, they shall receive business management training and financial support to expand their agricultural activities and enhance their role in the project.
In addition NRC conducted analytical work including: a comprehensive assessment in White Nile to identify the key HLP challenges facing displaced communities; gender analysis have been conducted in South Kordofan and White Nile (Kosti and Rabak) to inform gender-sensitive and inclusive programming; NRC also conducted a mapping exercise to identify sustainable agro-pastoral livelihood options in South Kordofan, assessing the suitability and profitability of crop and livestock production relevant to the local context and; a Seed Security System Assessment has been conducted in White Nile (Kosti and Rabak) to assess the availability, accessibility, and quality of seeds in local markets. The objective was to identify gaps and risks in the seed supply chain, guide the design of the seed voucher intervention, and ensure farmers could access timely and appropriate inputs for the planting season.
Challenges and lessons learned
The project was originally designed in a relatively stable context. However, the outbreak of conflict drastically shifted the environment to an emergency setting, severely affecting implementation and program activities that were prioritized. Activities requiring institutional presence, such as civil registry services in South Kordofan crucial for ICLA legal identity documentation, were not feasible due to government office closures. Consequently, NRC reallocated project resources to similar target populations in more conducive areas, ensuring continuity and impact.
In White Nile, market support faced challenges due to cash liquidity constraints. Despite functioning markets, assistance was shifted to vouchers or in-kind support, limiting the flexibility of goods available to beneficiaries. NRC partnered with a Financial Service Provider to establish a vendor network and implement a voucher platform to deliver market-based assistance effectively. Some delays in project approvals and the signing of Technical Agreements and MoUs reduced the available implementation window.
A particularly successful adaptation was the recruitment and training of male and female IDP paralegals from both displacement sites and host communities. These individuals provided consistent legal assistance even during access challenges and enhanced trust and local ownership.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
